preamble: The palatal lateral [ʎ] can lose its laterality and become the voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ]. In the medieval period, [ʎ] from Vulgar Latin -LJ-, -C'L-, -G'L- fricativized to Old Spanish /ʒ/ (later /ʃ/, then modern /x/), while Portuguese kept the lateral (filho, olho).

examples.note: The sound later devoiced to /ʃ/ and backed to modern /x/.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). History of the Spanish language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Spanish_language
